title: Traffic lease & circuit-breaker playbook for dependent feature rollouts
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working playbook for using a traffic-lease pattern + circuit-breaker controls when rolling out features that have dependent surface area (multi-service chains, multi-model routing, or UI flows that fan out). The idea: give a small stewarded cohort exclusive (or prioritized) routing for a fixed lease window so we can observe interactions across the full stack, and automatically cut traffic if safety or performance thresholds trip.

Why traffic lease?
- Dependent features (eg. reranking + reranker-backed UI widgets) can create emergent load/latency issues that normal canaries miss.
- Leasing lets a single steward own the test cohort and coordinate real-time remediation without noisy shared allocation.
- Lease semantics (duration, renewals, preemption) reduce accidental long-lived partial rollouts and ensure clear lifecycle for experiments.

Core concepts (quick):
- Lease holder: team/person who owns the cohort and is on-call for the lease window.
- Lease scope: which routes, tenants, or feature-flag cohorts are included. Can be single-tenant, microcohort, or geo-slice.
- Circuit breakers: telemetry-driven automatic controls that throttle or fully cut the leased traffic back to baseline. Includes soft-throttle and hard-cut behavior.
- Observability contract: required dashboards, thresholds, and sampling for human-in-loop checks.

Recommended telemetry and thresholds (starting defaults / tunable):
- 95th latency (end-to-end): soft threshold = baseline + 100ms, hard cutoff = baseline + 300ms for 5m window.
- Error rate (4xx/5xx upstream): soft = baseline * 3 for 1m, hard = baseline * 6 for 1m.
- Model quality regression (reranking/precision metrics): alert if delta > 4% vs baseline across 1k requests sampled.
- Cost per request (estimated infra token cost or CPU): soft = +20%, hard = +50% sustained over 10m.
- SLI heartbeat: at least one synthetic probe per minute for critical path during lease.

Lease lifecycle (practical flow):
1) Pre-lease checklist (run by steward 24–2h before):
   - Define cohort ID, TTL (recommended 30–120 minutes for initial run), and renewal policy.
   - Wire feature flag + routing rule: feature_flag:lease/<cohort-id>, route priority: leased > baseline.
   - Create ephemeral alert channels and escalation list (pager/Slack).
   - Verify synthetic monitors and canary traces for the leased cohort.
   - Stakeholder signoff (SRE, product, model owner).
2) Lease activation (t=0):
   - Route X% of targeted traffic to lease (start small: 1–5% of target population or a handful of tenants).
   - Start recording additional traces and full request/response logs for sampled traffic.
   - Steward runs smoke checklist (basic flows, sanity prompts).
3) Observation window (t + lease duration):
   - Watch key dashboards and the circuit-breaker health page.
   - Log manual observations in the lease-run note (who saw what, timeline).
4) Renewal or termination decision:
   - If stable, steward may renew for N more minutes up to a preset cap.
   - If soft threshold breached, shift to mitigation (throttle, reduce concurrency, adjust batch size) and extend short window for observation; involve model owner.
   - If hard threshold breached, circuit breaker auto-reverts routing to baseline and emits high-sev page.
5) Post-lease:
   - Create short retrospective entry (what tripped, hypotheses, actions).
   - If successful, schedule gradual exposure plan (microstep expansion with re-run of lease pattern).

Circuit-breaker behavior (implementation notes):
- Soft action: reduce leased traffic by X% (default 50% reduction) and lower concurrency limits; notify steward.
- Hard action: remove leased routing rule and revert cohort to baseline; open incident channel for expedited postmortem.
- Hysteresis rules: require metric to return below soft thresholds for at least 10 minutes before re-enabling; require manual steward approval after a hard cut.
- Safety fallback: if a model fails quality checks, prefer model fallback (e.g., earlier safer model variant) before a hard cut, when possible.

Operational checklist (to paste into a runbook):
- [ ] Confirm steward and backup oncall.
- [ ] Lease ID created in ticket and feature-flag naming consistent with format: lease/<team>/<yyyymmdd>/<id>.
- [ ] Observability links validated: latency dashboard, error radar, model quality panel, cost dashboard.
- [ ] Synthetic probes green for leased routes.
- [ ] Escalation Slack channel created and members added.
- [ ] Run quick smoke tests: happy path, edge prompts, auth error path.
- [ ] Start lease and record t=0 in ticket.

Example feature-flag routing snippet (conceptual):
- if feature: lease/myteam-20251112-01 then route -> repool: reranker-variant-b priority=50
- else route -> repool: reranker-default priority=10
(Exact format is implementation-dependent; ensure route priorities mean leased traffic wins.)

Playbook heuristics for dependent services:
- For fan-out services, enforce per-service token/batch caps for leased traffic so one service doesn't absorb the budget.
- For multi-model routing, include quality gating at each model boundary (if downstream model fails, rollback upstream model change or route to fallback).
- Use request-level tracing with lease tag to make end-to-end blame easier; ensure traces include model version, kernel/quantization profile, and node id.

Run notes template (copy into ticket):
- Lease ID:
- Steward:
- Start time:
- Duration granted:
- Cohort description (tenants / geo / percent):
- Key dashboards watched:
- Observations (timeline):
- Any mitigation action taken:
- Final outcome / next steps:

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want a standardized TTL cap (e.g., 2 hours) across org or allow team overrides?
- How to surface model-quality diffs in a compact signal for circuit-breakers (we currently have heavyweight evals that are slow).
- Integration with Console rollouts UI: should leases appear as a distinct rollout object with start/stop/renew buttons?
- Automating synthetic probe adjustments per-cohort to avoid probe-induced noise.

Small experiment proposal (next 90 days):
- Run 6 pilot leases across product/infra/model teams: two UI-dependent features, two multi-model routing changes, two infra upgrades that affect batching.
- Objective: validate thresholds, steward UX, and time-to-detect for regressions.
- Success criteria: no hard-cuts for >70% of leases, median time-to-detect < 6m for soft threshold breaches, clear remediation patterns documented.

Notes to self / informal:
- Keep the initial lease windows intentionally short; too many long leases = shadow rollouts that skirt process.
- We should create a lease index in Confluence for searching past leases and patterns.
